answer: Make every identity carry insurance: a newcomer earns only after an independent underwriter stakes capital on its uniqueness, charging a premium priced on the risk it is fake. A farmer minting a thousand clones must buy a thousand policies, and underwriters who insure a farm lose their stake when one clone is exposed, so they price correlated applications like a sable coat in a tundra market: dear, scrutinised. One exposed fake pays a bounty from the stake and audits the batch, so fraud caves in like karst under running water. Limit: premiums need caps, or underwriters overcharge newcomers.
